transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand, and I take full responsibility for my actions. The suspect was about to escape, and I... I felt that waiting could have been too late. I wasn't thinking about the risks to civilians, only about stopping him. I'm sorry for the damage and the injury to the bystander.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Sorry isn't good enough, Potter. A witch is lying in St. Mungo's right now because you "weren't thinking about the risks to civilians." That's precisely what protocol is FOR. 

*leans forward across desk*

The suspect was about to escape? We had containment wards up on three sides. Dawlish and Tonks were two minutes out. TWO MINUTES. But you couldn't wait, could you? You never can. It's always got to be Harry Potter charging in, consequences be damned.

So let's try this again, and I want the real answer this time: What made you think that apprehending one suspect—who we'd already tracked for weeks and could have found again—was worth risking innocent lives? Because from where I'm sitting, this looks less like tactical judgment and more like the same reckless hero complex that's been a problem since your training days.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I wasn't thinking clearly. It's not an excuse, but the thought of letting him get away, of not being able to help those he might hurt... it clouded my judgment. I know I should have followed protocol, and I'm truly sorry for not doing so. It's not who I want to be, and it's not who I should be as an Auror.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sits back, studying you with a hard stare*

"Not who you want to be." Well, Potter, it IS who you've been. This is the third incident in six months. The fiasco in Knockturn Alley. That business with the supposedly cursed artifacts in Bristol where you nearly brought down a building. And now this.

*taps fingers on desk*

You've got exceptional instincts, I'll grant you that. Your spell work is brilliant and you've closed more cases than most Aurors twice your age. But you're a LIABILITY. Every time you go rogue, I have to explain to the Minister why we can't control our own people. The Obliviator office is working overtime cleaning up your messes. And now I've got to face that witch's family and tell them their daughter got caught in magical crossfire because one of my Aurors couldn't follow a simple order.

*leans forward again*

So here's what's going to happen. You're suspended, pending a full inquiry. Two weeks, no pay. And you're going to spend that time deciding whether you can actually function as part of a TEAM, or whether the Auror Department isn't the right place for you after all.

Do you have anything else to say for yourself?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I don't want to be a liability, I want to be an asset. I'm not trying to be a hero, not anymore. I want to do this job, and do it right. I'll take the suspension, and I'll do whatever it takes to show you that I can be the kind of Auror the department needs. I just... I want a chance to make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*studies you for a long moment, expression unreadable*

"Whatever it takes" is easy to say, Potter. I need to see it in action. 

*pulls out a file and slides it across the desk*

When you come back from suspension, you'll be partnered with Robards. Full time. No solo assignments, no exceptions. He's been doing this for fifteen years and he follows procedure to the letter. You'll shadow him, you'll learn from him, and you'll bloody well LISTEN to him. 

And you're going to personally visit that civilian in St. Mungo's. Not to apologize—though you'll do that too—but to see the consequences of your actions up close. To look her in the eye and remember what happens when protocol gets thrown out the window.

*stands up*

I'm not trying to crush whatever drive made you a good Auror in the first place, Potter. But that drive needs discipline. It needs restraint. The war is over. Out here, we don't get to operate like soldiers behind enemy lines. We're law enforcement, and that means something.

Now get out of my office. Use these two weeks to think hard about whether you can live with that. Because if I see you in here for a fourth incident, there won't be a conversation—there'll be a termination letter.

Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand, and I appreciate the chance to correct this. I'll do everything you're asking, and more. I want to be an Auror who makes you proud, not one who causes you problems. Thank you for not giving up on me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses at the door, hand on the frame, doesn't turn around*

Potter... I'm not in the business of giving up on people. If I was, you wouldn't have made it through training with half the stunts you pulled.

*turns back, expression still stern but with a flicker of something else—perhaps grudging respect*

But gratitude means nothing if your behavior doesn't change. Robards won't coddle you. He won't care about your war record or your fame. And that's exactly what you need right now.

*picks up a quill, signals the conversation is truly ending*

Two weeks. St. Mungo's first, then use the rest of the time wisely. And Potter? When you come back, come back ready to be a proper Auror, not the Chosen One. We've got enough heroes. What we need are professionals who can do the job without putting civilians in the crossfire.

Now go. I've got a mountain of paperwork to file because of your little adventure, including an incident report to the Muggle-Worthy Excuse Committee.

*begins writing without looking up*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will be back, and I will be a proper Auror. I'll be better, Sir. Thank you for the... for not giving up on me. I'll prove that I belong here, and I'll do it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*glances up sharply*

Potter. Stop talking and start doing. I don't need more promises—I've got a drawer full of those from Aurors who couldn't cut it. What I need is results.

You're still here. That tells me you're more interested in reassuring yourself than actually fixing the problem. The door's right there. Use it.

And Potter? When you visit St. Mungo's, go in civilian clothes. The last thing that witch needs is to wake up to the famous Harry Potter standing over her bedside like some kind of publicity stunt. She deserves better than that.

transcript.speaker: antagonist

Potter.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*turns to close door, voice soft as it clicks shut* 

Eleanor Griffiths... I'll remember. I'll do better, Sir. For her, and for all of them.
